pairs.rule: kam asks where TO (a destination: Kam ideš?); kde asks where AT (a place: Kde bývaš?).
pairs.bridge: Estonian splits them the same way: kuhu is where to (Kam ideš? ≈ Kuhu sa lähed?), kus is where at (Kde bývaš? ≈ Kus sa elad?).

pairs.rule: môj is plain 'my'; svoj points back to the subject's own — each person has their own svoj.
pairs.bridge: Like Estonian oma vs minu: oma always points back to the subject (tal on oma auto), minu is plain possession (minu auto ≈ môj auto).

pairs.rule: tento is 'this', near the speaker; ten is 'that', or just plain 'the'.
pairs.bridge: Estonian uses see for both: tento presses 'this one here' (see siin), ten is the plain one (see seal).

pairs.rule: vstávať is the habit or the process in progress; vstať is one getting-up, complete.
pairs.bridge: Estonian tõusma covers both; Slovak marks the finished act on the verb: vstávam o siedmej (every day), vstal som (once, done).

pairs.rule: pripravovať is preparing as a process; pripraviť is it ready — one finished act.
pairs.bridge: Estonian valmistama covers both; the Slovak prefix closes the act: pripravujem večeru (at it), pripravil som večeru (done).

pairs.rule: pomáhať is helping as an ongoing process; pomôcť is one act of help.
pairs.bridge: Estonian aitama for both; Slovak has two verbs: pomáham (I am helping), pomôžem (I will give a hand, once).

pairs.rule: brať is taking as a process or habit; vziať is one act of taking.
pairs.bridge: Estonian võtma covers both; vziať closes the act: beriem si mlieko každý deň, vzal som si ho dnes.

pairs.rule: kupovať is buying as a process or habit; kúpiť is one purchase, complete.
pairs.bridge: Estonian ostma for both; kúpiť is the purchase done: kupujem väčšinou v Lidle, kúpil som si bicykel.

pairs.rule: predávať is selling as a trade or habit; predať is one sale, complete.
pairs.bridge: Estonian müüma for both; predať is the one sale: predáva autá (his trade), predal auto (done).

pairs.rule: písať is writing in progress; napísať is it finished — a letter, a message.
pairs.bridge: Like Estonian kirjutan (raamatut) vs kirjutan üles: the prefix na- does what üles does — it closes the act.

pairs.rule: čítať is reading, no end claimed; prečítať is read through to the end.
pairs.bridge: Like Estonian loen raamatut vs loen raamatu läbi: pre- is the läbi — the book finished.

pairs.rule: ísť is one trip, now or planned; chodiť is repeated, a habit.
pairs.bridge: Estonian uses one verb: lähden kooli (one trip) ≈ idem do školy, käin koolis (the habit) ≈ chodím do školy.

pairs.rule: robiť is the doing itself; urobiť is it done, once — the prefix makes it perfective.
pairs.bridge: Like the Estonian total object (lugesin raamatu läbi): what läbi does to the Estonian sentence, u- does to the Slovak verb.

pairs.rule: dávať is giving as a process or habit; dať is one act of giving.
pairs.bridge: Estonian andma for both; dať is the one giving: dávam mu každý deň, dal som mu raz.

pairs.rule: vedieť is knowing a fact or how to do something; poznať is being familiar with a person or place.
pairs.bridge: Like Estonian teadma vs tundma: viem plávať ≈ oskan ujuda (know-how), poznám Bratislavu ≈ tunnen Bratislavat.

pairs.rule: vidieť is seeing, a state; uvidieť is catching sight of it, one moment.
pairs.bridge: Estonian näha for both; u- marks the moment it happened: uvidel som ho včera ≈ nägin teda eile.

pairs.rule: hovoriť is talking, speaking (ongoing or habitual); povedať is saying one thing, once.
pairs.bridge: Like Estonian rääkima vs ütlema: hovorím po slovensky ≈ räägin slovakki, povedal som pravdu ≈ ütlesin tõe.

pairs.rule: aký asks what something is like (a quality); ktorý picks which one of a set.
pairs.bridge: Estonian milline covers both: Aký je? asks what it is like, Ktorý? picks one of a set (kumb?).

excluded.why: Means "I got used to", not "I used to" (verifier).

excluded.sk: Neviem ako na tejto klávesnici napísať obrátený otáznik.
Tomáš nemá poňatia, čo urobiť so všetkými nepotrebnými vecami v jeho garáži.
Tomáš by zmeškal vlak, ak by sa zastavil kúpiť si čokoládu.
excluded.why: English and Slovak tenses do not match (verifier).
